Name: a2val_fixed_seed_replication_ablation_sensitivity_round2
Title: Executed Fixed-Seed Replication, Ablation, and Sensitivity Audit for A2 Conditional Controls
Short Hypothesis: The prior round only verified the package environment and inventory. This revision tests the core empirical claim directly by re-executing the existing a2val E1/E2/E3/E5 and optional physical-tangent scripts under a fixed seed matrix, adding the four planned baseline ablation runners and negative-control/threshold sweeps, and reporting seed-level CIs, ablation deltas, sensitivity boundaries, and an explicit missing-run ledger. It does not introduce a new algorithm, model, or hardware claim.
Related Work: Projections, Schur complements, coherent calibration, variable projection, source extension, continuation, and experiment design remain prior machinery. The workdir already contains the a2val implementation, run scripts, previous JSON/CSV artifacts, figures, tests, and a validated venv. This revision continues the completed environment/inventory stage by converting the existing package into an executed fixed-seed replication and ablation study rather than relying on prior summary artifacts.
Abstract: We revise the A2 audit from an inventory-only round into an executed robustness study. The existing a2val modules are re-run under a fixed seed matrix, and all evidence metrics are recomputed from newly generated raw JSON/CSV artifacts rather than from prior summaries. The revision adds a lightweight runner for E1/E2/E3/E5 and the optional physical-tangent script, plus four ablation scripts: physical versus free-current envelope, relative-only versus absolute/bias-aware gates, shared-map versus independent-map profiling, and greedy versus pair lookahead. Negative controls and threshold sweeps over noise level, rank threshold, and gate threshold are generated from existing modules to measure false-positive modes and boundary sensitivity. The study reports seed counts, Monte Carlo sample sizes, runtimes, 95% Student-t CIs, replication pass/fail, ablation deltas, and sensitivity tables. Controls that cannot be supported by the existing parameterization are placed in an explicit not-run ledger with reasons. Claims remain limited to synthetic conditional controls; E4, nonlinear superiority, SOM exclusivity, universal basin behavior, and publication acceptance are not claimed unless a corresponding runner is executed.

datasets: Existing A2 E1 scalar matched complex/intensity exact examples, re-executed from e1.py under the fixed seed matrix
Existing A2 E2/E3/E5 exact and random fixed-tangent examples, re-executed from e2.py/e3.py/e5.py under the fixed seed matrix
Synthetic noise-level, rank-threshold, and gate-threshold sweep sets generated from existing a2val modules
Optional physical tangent cases from the existing shared-core physical_runner.py, treated only as secondary corroboration
Negative-control and not-run ledger artifacts generated by existing modules or recorded as unsupported
baselines: relative-only versus absolute and bias-aware gate ablation
greedy versus pair lookahead acquisition ablation
negative controls and no-sweep baseline artifacts from existing modules
limited-aperture tangent and nearly-parallel-range controls if supported by existing parameters, otherwise recorded as not run
metrics: number of successful fixed-seed executions per module, seed count, Monte Carlo sample size, and wall-clock runtime
backward-error-scaled identity residual mean, standard deviation, and 95% Student-t confidence interval across fixed-seed reruns
Fisher contraction ratio with Monte Carlo confidence intervals
covariance and bias risk ratios versus absolute and relative gates
acquisition innovation gain, submodularity violation count, and greedy-versus-lookahead delta
threshold-sweep pass boundaries, false-positive/false-negative rates, and rank/noise sensitivity tables
replication pass/fail per metric under a predetermined tolerance, plus raw artifact existence and discrepancy ledger
Experiments.compute_estimate: Small CPU-only NumPy/SciPy using the already validated venv. The runner and sweeps are capped by a max_seeds and max_sweeps config in the new scripts; expected workload is re-executing the existing small synthetic package under a fixed seed matrix plus bounded sweeps. No GPU, no new installation, and no new large-scale dataset is required.
steps: Inventory command-line or config-exposed parameters for e1.py/e2.py/e3.py/e5.py and physical_runner.py; record which seed, noise level, rank threshold, and gate threshold arguments can be set externally.

Add and run a fixed-seed matrix runner that actually executes E1/E2/E3/E5 and optional physical tangent, writing one raw JSON/CSV artifact per seed and a summary manifest containing seed count, runtime, and Monte Carlo sample size.

Recompute all primary evidence metrics from the newly generated raw artifacts only; do not reuse prior summary CSVs as evidence; report seed-level 95% Student-t CIs and replication pass/fail with explicit tolerance.
Implement the four planned baseline ablation scripts as separate runners that write raw JSON/CSV and compact comparison tables, recording each delta and direction.
Run negative controls and threshold sweeps using existing modules over noise level, rank threshold, and gate threshold; classify false-positive modes and identify where conclusions change.

Attempt limited-aperture tangent and nearly-parallel-range controls if the existing modules expose the required parameters; otherwise write an explicit not-run ledger with reasons and expected missing outputs.
Write a revised quantitative supplement with actual artifact paths, raw-to-summary provenance, replication/ablation/sensitivity tables, and all discrepancies or unsupported claims explicitly marked.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The prior round produced no new raw rerun artifacts, so this revision is the first substantive execution; seed-level failures or parameter mismatches may appear and must be reported honestly.
Some planned ablations or controls may be unsupported by the existing a2val functions; those will be placed in an explicit not-run ledger rather than inferred from old artifacts.
The synthetic validation suite may still be underpowered for a full ACL Rolling Review paper even after fixed-seed re-execution and sensitivity analysis.

Exact identities and near-zero residuals can be vacuous sanity checks if negative controls are weak; negative-control and boundary-sweep results are intended to bound this risk but cannot eliminate it.
The optional physical-tangent run remains secondary corroboration and may be too weak for strong physical claims.

No claim is made about E4 primary comparison, nonlinear superiority, SOM exclusivity, universal basin behavior, or publication acceptance unless a corresponding runner is executed in the same workdir.
